boe-2026-09.standing: The Bank of England's Monetary Policy Committee, whose nine members vote individually on Bank Rate at eight scheduled meetings a year. The rate they set feeds through to British mortgages, business borrowing and the pound.
boe-2026-09.recent: The vote comes a day after the Fed raised rates unanimously, and for the same reason: a closed strait, with Brent crude near $110 a barrel. That leaves this committee the question Washington has already answered its own way — whether to look through a supply shock monetary policy cannot reach, or tighten into it regardless.

boj-2026-09.standing: Japan's central bank, whose policy board meets eight times a year to set the short-term policy rate and steer government bond yields. It anchors borrowing costs in the world's largest creditor nation, and the yen moves with it.
boj-2026-09.recent: Tokyo has been weighing whether to steer the currency through pension money — a yen defence run outside the central bank entirely — and the yen has since surged as the dollar slid to its weakest since May. That leaves the board's own instrument, the policy rate, as what this meeting settles.

uk-cpi-2026-10.standing: The UK's monthly consumer price index, compiled by the Office for National Statistics. It is the measure the Bank of England's inflation target is written against, and it feeds index-linked gilts, pensions and a range of regulated prices.
uk-cpi-2026-10.recent: This release settles what UK consumer prices did in September, in a single figure published in one go. Nothing on the record yet marks it out from a routine month.

fomc-2026-10.standing: The Federal Open Market Committee, the twelve-member body that meets eight times a year to set the US federal funds rate. Because the dollar prices most cross-border borrowing, what it decides reaches far past American borders.
fomc-2026-10.recent: The committee voted 12-0 on September 16 to tighten into a supply shock it cannot reach — the closure of a strait after Houthi forces took Yemen's port of Mocha. August consumer prices rose 0.4%. October settles whether Kevin Warsh's Fed keeps raising while the cause sits outside its reach, and dollar borrowers pay for the answer.

ecb-2026-10.standing: The Governing Council of the European Central Bank, which sets the policy rate for every country that shares the euro at meetings roughly six weeks apart. One decision fixes the cost of credit across a single currency and many separate fiscal policies.
ecb-2026-10.recent: Deutsche Bank has moved its projected ECB peak to 2.75%, reading the energy shock as feeding second-round effects rather than passing through. The Fed has already tightened into the same closed strait, 12-0. What this meeting settles is whether the ECB treats Brent near $110 as a shock to look through, or one already lodged in wages and prices.

boj-2026-10.standing: Japan's central bank, whose policy board meets eight times a year to set the short-term rate. Decades of near-zero policy made the yen the world's cheapest funding currency, so its settings reach borrowers well outside Japan.
boj-2026-10.recent: Tokyo has been weighing whether to steer the yen with pension money — a sign that the currency, not consumer prices, is the pressure the board is sitting under. The Fed has moved the other way and raised, widening the gap the yen falls through, and this meeting settles whether Japan answers with the policy rate or leaves the defence to other hands.

boe-2026-11.standing: The Bank of England's nine-member Monetary Policy Committee meets eight times a year to set Bank Rate, the floor under British mortgage and business borrowing. Its votes are published individually, and sterling moves with them.
boe-2026-11.recent: This is the committee's first meeting since the Federal Reserve raised rates 12-0 into a supply shock it cannot reach — a closed strait, Brent crude near $110 a barrel. The same argument arrives here: whether to look through a fuel price monetary policy cannot produce, or tighten against everything else until the average holds.

fomc-2026-12.standing: The Federal Open Market Committee, which sets the US federal funds rate at eight scheduled meetings a year and publishes members' rate projections alongside the decision. Dollar borrowing costs worldwide move with it.
fomc-2026-12.recent: September's move was unanimous, 12-0, and the cause was a closed strait — tightening into a supply shock that monetary policy cannot reach. Chair Kevin Warsh reads the 19-year high in bond yields as economic strength and borrowing demand, not lost confidence in the inflation fight. This meeting tests that with Brent near $110.

g20-2026-miami.standing: The annual meeting of heads of state and government from the world's largest economies, plus the European Union. It has no treaty powers, so its weight rests on what the leaders in the room agree to say and do together on debt, trade, energy and war.

ecb-2026-12.standing: The European Central Bank's Governing Council, which meets eight times a year to set one interest rate for the entire euro area. It fixes the cost of credit from Germany to Greece, and sovereign borrowing spreads move with it.
ecb-2026-12.recent: Deutsche Bank has raised where it expects the ECB's tightening to end to 2.75%, on the argument that the energy shock is passing into second-round wage and price effects rather than fading out. With Brent near $110 a barrel, what this Council is weighing is whether an import bill it cannot influence has now embedded itself in domestic costs.

boe-2026-12.standing: The Bank of England's Monetary Policy Committee, whose members vote individually eight times a year to set Bank Rate. It sets what mortgages, business loans and savings pay across the UK, and sterling moves with it.
boe-2026-12.recent: The Committee meets with Brent crude near $110 a barrel — an imported cost the policy rate cannot reach, because monetary policy suppresses demand and cannot produce a barrel of oil. The decision settles whether the Bank of England looks through a supply shock or leans against it, and every member's vote is published.

boj-2026-12.standing: The Bank of Japan's policy board, which meets eight times a year to set Japan's short-term policy rate. Decades of near-zero rates made the yen the world's cheap funding currency, so carry trades built abroad unwind when it moves.
boj-2026-12.recent: Tokyo has been weighing whether to steer the yen with pension money — an admission that the currency question has outgrown the tools the board normally reaches for. The Fed has since raised rates in a unanimous vote, widening the gap the yen trades on. What this meeting settles is whether the policy rate, not the pension fund, does the defending.
